newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Jan car sales plunge on strikes.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Jan car sales plunge on strikes.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's largest carmaker, said on Tuesday its vehicle sales plunged to 48,432 units in January from 106,885 a year ago.
A company spokesman said the drop was due largely to strikes that lasted for about a month, ending January 20.
Hyundai spokesman Min Kyung-hwan said exports in the month totalled 16,768 units, down sharply from 43,818 a year ago.
"Strikes between December 26 and January 20 cost the company about 80,000 units in lost production," Min said.

Workers at some of the nation's major industries walked out in protest at the ruling party which forced a controversial labour law through parliament making it easier for companies to lay off workers.
In 1996, Hyundai Motor sold a total of 1.31 million units, up from 1.23 million units the previous year.
Hyundai has set this year's sales target at 1.45 million units, of which 650,000 are for export.
Min said weakening local consumer demand as a result of an economic downturn also contributed to the January sales fall.
